text:
Sasha: Heads-up — since ~01:10 UTC we're seeing a sharp spike in outbound connection failures from edge proxy pods in eu-west-1. Model pulls and inference outbound calls are getting 502s / connection resets. Logs attached below. :eyes:
Kai: Yep, CloudWatch shows NATGateway ActiveConnections near the per-NAT limit in the eu-west-1a AZ. Looks like ephemeral port exhaustion pattern. Which rollout triggered extra pulls?
Sasha: Recent rollout to increase prewarm model fetches. Reverting now but wanted to call out mitigation ideas. Sample netstat from one sidecar:
```
Proto Recv-Q Send-Q Local Address           Foreign Address         State      
tcp        0      0 10.0.5.12:45231        52.216.12.34:443       TIME_WAIT
tcp        0      0 10.0.5.12:45232        52.216.12.35:443       TIME_WAIT
tcp        0      0 10.0.5.12:45233        52.216.12.36:443       TIME_WAIT
```
Marco: Sounds similar to the fanout we saw last quarter but different AZ distribution. We had sidecars spawning 40-60 parallel fetches per node.
Priya: Confirmed — yesterday's sidecar config bumped max_concurrent_model_fetches to 50 for faster cold start. That probably blew up ephemeral port banks when scaled to 200 nodes.
Nate: Observability: we're also seeing tokenization latency spikes as clients retry. Cost note — retries double egress bytes and increase per-token infra cost.
OpsBot: deploy-bot: rollback candidate available (deploy 2026-03-18T01:12Z) — initiated canary.
Kai: Immediate mitigations we can do now (ordered):
- reduce model fetch parallelism -> 6-8 per sidecar
- enable keepalive and connection reuse at HTTP client layer (50s-90s)
- route model-store traffic via S3 VPC endpoint to bypass NAT
- add ephemeral port monitoring alert (TIME_WAIT > threshold)
Also consider provisioning additional NAT Gateway Elastic IPs in the busiest AZs to raise port entropy.
Sasha: Rolling a patch to cap fetch concurrency to 6 in eu-west-1 now. Will watch for error rates and NAT metrics. :thumbsup:
Priya: Low-effort quick win: add S3 Gateway/VPC endpoint for the model bucket(s) so fetches don't hit NAT. We'll open a PR.
Marco: Mid-term: implement a regional model-fetch cache (shared local proxy) so only one node fetches an image and serves cached bytes to pods. That reduces egress fanout massively.
Nate: Cost tradeoffs: extra NAT Gateways per AZ ~ ~$2-4k/mo each (rough estimate). Running a small fleet of pooling proxies (t3.small + autoscale) might be cheaper but adds operational burden. I'll do a cost comparison.
Kai: Also explore using AWS Gateway Load Balancer + a pooling proxy appliance we manage — gives us connection pooling and more controlled source port reuse.
Sasha: Monitoring tasks: creating a dashboard with these metrics:
- ephemeral port usage per NAT (approx via ActiveConnections / port range)
- per-pod TIME_WAIT counts
- model-fetch concurrency per sidecar
- NATGateway errors and 5xx rates
I'll add an alert: ephemeral_ports_utilization > 80% for > 5m = paging.
Nate: I'll open the postmortem skeleton — include timeline, changed config, delta in concurrent fetches, and mitigation timeline.
Priya: Will submit the S3 endpoint PR and a small sidecar rollback PR (concurrency -> 6).
Marco: After rollback, let's keep a soft cap in config so teams can't accidentally bump it again without perf signoff.
Sasha: Thanks all — rolling now. If anyone sees new 5xxs mention @Sasha and I'll escalate. :rocket:
